chapter: The Legends of Jazz and life on the road
title: The 1974 European tour
summary: The February tour is marred by illness, with Joe Darensbourg sent home from London, and the band stays in cheap hotels.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Very good. We didn't got to Europe until the next year, February, and this was in September when we made the New England tour and we came back home. In February, we also made a partial tour of the states and

Europe. This is when I almost didn't make, I almost caught a cold and almost didn't make it and Joe Darenbourg didn't make. When he got to London he had a touch of pneumonia and had to be sent back home.
Then there was this boy that looked like a girl--
I showed you a picture there of the band.
Oh, I don't remember who that was.
From London we went onto Germany, Belgium, Sweden, Denmark, and came back in March, I think.
Did you meet many of the European musicians?
Did they sit in with you?
No, they didn't sit in with us.
They were just so honored to be in your presence I'm sure.
We were playing concerts, you know, so we couldn't have sit-ins.
Sometimes we'd go to a party and they'd sit in; once in a while but very seldom because everybody was tired after a concert.

Accommodations weren't so good our first trip over, because Barry had just started out, he didn't have too much money /and so we stayed in the cheapest hotels, but later one we changed that. We all have singles now, nobody doubles anymore. That was '74.
